Will they not then be thankful?﴾ ﴿Glory be to He who created all the pairs, from what the earth grows, and from themselves, and from what they do not know.﴾ ﴿And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and at once they are in darkness.﴾ ﴿And the sun runs toward its resting place. That is the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿And the moon, We have determined for it stations until it returns like the old dry palm stalk.﴾ ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; and each is floating in an orbit.﴾ ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship,﴾ ﴿and We created for them of its like that which they ride.﴾ ﴿And if We will, We drown them, and there is no one to call for help, nor are they rescued,﴾ ﴿except as mercy from Us and enjoyment for a time.﴾ ﴿And when it is said to them, "Fear what is before you and what is behind you, that you may be shown mercy,"﴾ ﴿no sign from the signs of their Lord comes to them but that they turn away from it.﴾ ﴿And when it is said to them, "Spend from what God has provided you," those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Shall we feed one whom God would have fed if He willed? You are only in clear error."﴾ ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ ﴿They await only a single cry that will seize them while they are disputing.﴾ ﴿So they will not be able to make a bequest, nor return to their families.﴾ ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and at once they will rush from the graves to their Lord.﴾ ﴿They will say, "Woe to us! Who has raised us from our resting place? This is what the Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth."﴾ ﴿It will be but one cry, and at once they will all be brought before Us.﴾ ﴿So today no soul will be wronged in anything, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in delight,﴾ ﴿they and their spouses, in shade, reclining on couches.﴾ ﴿For them therein is fruit, and for them is whatever they call for.﴾ ﴿"Peace!" a word from a Lord, Most Merciful.﴾ (p. 322) ﴿"And stand apart today, O guilty ones.﴾ ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is a clear enemy to you,﴾ ﴿and that you should worship Me? This is a straight path.﴾ ﴿And he had already led astray a great multitude among you. Did you not then use reason?﴾ ﴿This is Hell, which you were promised.﴾ ﴿Burn therein today for what you used to disbelieve.﴾ ﴿Today We seal their mouths, and their hands speak to Us, and their feet bear witness to what they used to earn.﴾ ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes, and they would race for the path; but how could they see?﴾ ﴿And if We willed, We would have transformed them in their places, so they would not be able to proceed or return.﴾ ﴿And whomever We let live long, We reverse him in creation. Will they not then understand?﴾ ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it suitable for him. It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an,﴾ ﴿to warn whoever is alive, and that the word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿Do they not see that We have created for them, from what Our hands have made, cattle, and they are their owners?﴾ ﴿And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat.﴾ ﴿And for them in them are benefits and drinks. Will they not then be thankful?﴾ ﴿And they have taken gods besides God, hoping they might be helped.﴾ ﴿They cannot help them, and they are a mobilized host for them.﴾ ﴿So do not let their saying grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they reveal.﴾ ﴿Has not man seen that We created him from a drop, and then he is an open adversary?﴾ ﴿And he has struck for Us a parable and forgotten his creation. He said, "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ ﴿Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knower of all creation.﴾ ﴿He who made for you from the green tree fire, and then you kindle from it."﴾ ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Yes, indeed; He is the All-Creating, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ ﴿So glory be to He in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned.﴾

Qamaḥa al-ba'īru ra'sahu (قَمَحَ البَعِيرُ رَأْسَهُ): he raised his head, after drinking water; the discussion of it will come in full. Al-ʿurjūn (العُرْجُونُ): the stalk of the date cluster, from between the stem to its point of origin on the palm tree. Al-Zajjaj said: it is fuʿlūn, from al-inʿirāj, which is bending. Al-jadath (الجَدَثُ): the grave. It is also heard as jadaf, with the thāʾ replaced by fāʾ, as they said fumm for thumm; and as they replaced fāʾ with thāʾ, they said maʿthūr for maʿfūr. It is a kind of truffle. Al-maskh (المَسْخُ): transformation from one form into a hideous form. Al-ramīm (الرَّمِيمُ): decayed and crumbling.

* *

﴿Ya-Sin.﴾ ﴿By the Qur'an, full of wisdom,﴾ ﴿indeed you are among the messengers,﴾ ﴿upon a straight path.﴾ ﴿It is a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful,﴾ ﴿that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless.﴾ ﴿The word has certainly come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles around their necks, reaching to the chins, so they are held with their heads raised.﴾ ﴿And We have placed a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, and covered them, so they do not see.﴾ ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ ﴿You can only warn one who follows the Reminder and fears the Merciful in the unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and a noble reward.﴾ ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forth and their traces, and everything We have enumerated in a clear register.﴾.

This surah is Meccan, except that a group claimed that His words ﴿and We record what they have sent forth﴾ and "their traces" were revealed concerning the Banu Salama of the Ansar, when they wanted to leave their homes and move to be near the Mosque of the Messenger; but this claim is not correct. It is also said: except His words ﴿And when it is said to them, "Spend from what God has provided you"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 47] and the verse that follows.

The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. Ibn Jubayr said here: it is one of the names of Muhammad (ﷺ), and its evidence is ﴿indeed you are among the messengers﴾. Sayyid al-Hamawi said:

"O soul, do not purify yourself with love, striving for affection, except for the family of Yasin."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: its meaning is "O human" in Ethiopian (Habashi). And from him: it is in the dialect of Tayy, for they say īsān meaning insān, and they pluralize it as ayāsīn; so this is from it. Another group said: yā is a vocative particle, and the sīn stands in place of insān, from which a letter was removed and it was placed in its stead. Al-Zamakhshari said: if it is true that its meaning is "O human" in the dialect of Tayy, then its basis is to be ya-unaysīn, and the calling was so frequent on their tongues that they limited it to a part of it, as they said in the oath: mu-llāh and ayman-llāh. End of quote. What is reported from the Arabs in the diminutive of insān is unaysiyān, with a yāʾ followed by an alif, which indicates that its root is unaysān, because diminution returns things to their roots; and we do not know that they said its diminutive as unaysīn. And even on the assumption that it is a remnant of unaysīn, that is not permissible, neither being built on a ḍamma nor remaining pausal; because it is a vocative addressed directly, and also it is not permissible because it is a diminutive, and that is impermissible with regard to the prophethood. His saying "as they said in the oath mu-llāh and ayman-llāh" is one view. Among the grammarians there are those who say that mu is a particle of oath and is not a remnant of ayman.

It was read with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, with its pure imāla (inclination), and between the two pronunciations. The majority read with a sukūn on the nūn, assimilated into the wāw. Among the seven: al-Kisa'i, Abu Bakr, Warsh, and Ibn ʿAmir read it with clear pronunciation, while the rest of the seven read it as assimilated. Ibn Abi Ishaq and ʿIsa read with a fatḥa on the nūn. Qatada said: Yasin is an oath. Abu Hatim said: the analogy of this view is a fatḥa on the nūn, as you say: "Allāh, I will certainly do such-and-such." Al-Zajjaj said: a naṣb, as if he said: "Recite Yasin," and this is according to Sibawayh's view that it is a name for the surah. Al-Kalbi read with a ḍamma on the nūn, and said it is in the dialect of Tayy: "O human." Al-Sammak and Ibn Abi Ishaq also read with a kasra. It was said: the vowel is because of the meeting of two sukūns; the fatḥa is sought for lightness, the ḍamma like ḥaythu, and the kasra is on the basis of their meeting. If it is said that it is an oath, it may be in the naṣb position according to Abu Hatim's view, the rafʿ as a mubtada' (subject), like "the trust of God, I will surely stand," and the jarr by implying a particle of jarr, which is permissible according to the Kufans. (Al-Ḥakīm): either it is faʿīl in the sense of mufʿal, as you say: "I tied the honey, so it is ʿaqīd," meaning maʿqūd; or it is for emphasis from ḥākim; or it is in the sense of cause, that is, possessing wisdom.

﴿Upon a straight path﴾ is a second predicate, or it is in the position of a circumstantial clause from him, peace be upon him, or from "the messengers," or it is related to "the messengers." The straight path is the law of Islam.

Talha, al-Ashhab and ʿIsa read, according to the varying reports from them, tanzīla with a naṣb as a verbal noun; Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read tanzīla with a naṣb as a verbal noun; the rest of the seven, Abu Bakr, Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, al-Hasan, al-Aʿraj, and al-Aʿmash read it with a rafʿ as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: it is a revelation. Abu Ḥaywa, al-Yazidi, and al-Qursi from Abu Jaʿfar and Shayba read it with a jarr, either as an apposition to "the Qur'an," or as a description by a verbal noun. (Li-tundhira) is related to tanzīl or to arsalnā implied.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 36, verses 1–20 (part 2 of 2):

﴿What their fathers were warned of﴾. Ikrimah said: "mā" means "alladhī" (the one that), i.e., "the thing that their fathers were warned of, of the punishment." Then "mā" is the second object, as in His saying ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾ (al-Naba 78:40). Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: "It is also possible that mā is a verbal noun (maṣdariyyah), meaning ﴿what their fathers were warned﴾, and the fathers in this case are the earliest of the descendants of Ismaʿil, among whom warning had existed." And "fa-hum" (so they) according to this interpretation means "fa-innahum" (for they). The fāʾ is used to separate one clause from another clause that stands as a relative clause (ṣilah), so it connects to His saying ﴿Indeed, you are among the messengers﴾. The phrase "to warn" (li-tundhira) is like when you say: "I sent you to so-and-so to warn him, for he is heedless, or rather he is heedless." Qatadah said: "mā" is a negation, meaning that their fathers were not warned. In this case, "their fathers" are the nearer ones among them, and "mā undhira" is in the position of a qualifier, meaning "whose fathers were not warned." "Fa-hum ghafilūn" (so they are heedless) is connected to the negation, meaning: they were not warned, so they are heedless, since their not being warned is the cause of their heedlessness. By considering the fathers in terms of their antiquity and nearness, the contradiction between warning and its negation disappears.

﴿Indeed, the word has come into effect against most of them﴾. The well-known view is that the word is ﴿I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together﴾ (Hud 11:119). It was also said: it means that the necessity of punishment was already decreed in His knowledge. And it was said: "the word" (al-qawl) [p. 324] is what God said through the tongue of the messengers, concerning monotheism and other matters, and its proof became clear; so most of them do not believe after that. The apparent meaning of His saying ﴿Indeed, We have placed shackles upon their necks﴾ and what follows is that it is literal, not metaphorical (istiʿārah, metaphor). When God, exalted is He, stated that they do not believe, He then informed about some of their conditions in the Hereafter when they enter the Fire. Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: "His saying ﴿So We covered them, and they cannot see﴾ weakens this view, because the sight of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection is sharp, seeing the ugliness of their state." End of quote. But this does not weaken it. Do you not see His saying ﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind﴾ (al-Isra 17:97), and His saying ﴿He will say: My Lord, why have You gathered me blind?﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:125)? Or His saying ﴿So your sight today is sharp﴾ (Qaf 50:22) may be a kinayah (metonymy, allusion) for his grasp of what he is coming to, as if he sees it. The majority said: that is a metaphor. Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Ishaq said: it is a metaphor for the state of the disbelievers who intended harm to the Messenger; God made this an example for them in restraining them from him and preventing them from harming him when they plotted against him. Al-Ḍaḥḥak and al-Farrāʾ said: it is a metaphor for their withholding from spending in the way of God, as He said ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾ (al-Isra 17:29). Ikrimah said: it was revealed when Abu Jahl intended to strike him with a great stone, and in other such occasions, but God prevented him. This is close to the view of Ibn ʿAbbas. It is narrated that "Abu Jahl carried a stone to throw at the Prophet ﷺ while he was praying, and his hands were bent up to his neck, so that he returned to his companions with the stone stuck in his hand. They could not free it except with great effort. Then he took another stone, but when he approached the Messenger, God blinded his sight so he did not see him. He returned to his companions and could not see them until they called out to him." So the shackle becoming a metaphor refers to the restraint of Abu Jahl and others in this story. And since Abu Jahl's companions were content with what he intended to do, this was attributed to a group. Another group said: it is a metaphor for God's preventing them from faith and His placing a barrier between them and it. Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: this is the most preferred of the views, because when God mentioned that they do not believe, due to what had been decreed for them from eternity, He followed this with making for them a restraint and an encompassing wretchedness in which their state is like that of those who are shackled. End of quote. Al-Zamakhshari said: it is an image (tamthīl) of their insistence upon disbelief, and that there is no way to their claim of [being guided], as He made them like the shackled, head-raised (muqmaḥūn), in that they do not turn toward the truth, nor bend their necks toward it, nor lower their heads to it; and like those confined between two barriers, who see neither what is before them nor what is behind them, in that they have no reflection and do not see, meaning they are blind to considering the signs of God, exalted is He. End of quote. In his words there is a hidden trace of Muʿtazilism (dasīsat al-iʿtizāl). Do you not see that the statement of the People of the Sunnah (ahl al-sunnah, the orthodox majority) is "a metaphor for God's preventing them from faith," while al-Zamakhshari's statement is "an image of their insistence," and he attributes the actions that he counts to them and not to God? The ghull (shackle) is that which surrounds the neck, for the sake of rebuke, constriction, punishment, and captivity. With the neck, both hands or one hand [are bound], for the sake of explanation (taʿlīl). The apparent reference of the pronoun in "fa-hiya" (so they are) is to the shackles, because they are the ones mentioned and spoken of. Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: they are broad, reaching the chin with their edges, and the chin is the junction of the two jaws, so the shackled man is compelled to raise his face toward the sky, and that is iqmāḥ (raising the head with lowered gaze), which is close to the meaning of being held with a halter in appearance. Al-Zamakhshari said: the shackles, the origin of which is "up to the chins," are fastened to them. That is because the collar of the shackle, which is around the neck of the shackled one, has at the meeting of its two ends under the chin a ring in which the head of the post sits, passing through the ring up to the chin, so it does not let him lower his head or lay his nape down, so he remains always raising his head. End of quote. Al-Farrāʾ said: qamḥ is that in which one lowers his gaze after raising his head. Al-Zajjaj said something similar, saying: it is said "qamaḥa al-baʿīr raʾsahu ʿan rayy" (the camel raised its head away from water) and "qamaḥa" (it did so). Abu ʿUbayda said: qamaḥa qumūḥan: he raised his head from the pool without drinking, and the plural is qiṣāḥ (camels that raise their heads). From this is the saying of Bishr, describing the death of one of them so that they would bury him:

"We sit around its sides, lowering our gaze like camels with raised heads (qiṣāḥ)."

Al-Layth said: it is the raising of the camel's head when it drinks bad water, then it returns. Al-Zajjaj said: the two months of the winter (al-kānūnayn) are called "shahrā qimāḥ" because when camels come to water they raise their heads because of its extreme coldness. Abu Zayd recited the verse of al-Hudhali:

"A youth, the son of the mighty, when we pass the winter, and provisions are loved in the two months of qimāḥ."

He narrated it with a ḍamma on the qāf, and Ibn al-Sikkit with a kasra, and both are dialects. The two were called "the two months of qimāḥ" because every creature with a liver dislikes drinking water in them. Al-Ḥasan said: al-qāmiḥ is one who raises his gaze toward the place of his foot. Mujahid said: the one raising the head, the one placing his hand over his mouth. Al-Ṭabarī said: the pronoun in "fa-hiya" refers to the hands, even though no mention of them preceded, because its place is clear from the meaning, since the shackle is only on the neck with the two hands, which is why the shackle was named "jāmiʿah" (gatherer), for it gathers the hand and the neck. ʿAli, may God honor his face, saw people raising their heads, so he placed his hands under his jaws and pressed them and raised his head. Al-Zamakhshari said: he made the qimāḥ the result of His saying ﴿so they are up to the chins﴾. If the pronoun referred to the hands, the sense of causation in the qimāḥ would not be apparent; and this placement of a pronoun involves a kind of contrivance and abandoning of the apparent meaning, which the meaning itself calls for, toward falsehood, which turns away from the clear truth toward a confused falsehood. End of quote.

The reading of ʿAbd Allah, Ikrimah, al-Nakhaʿi, Ibn Wathhab, Talha, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Ibn Kathir and Ḥafṣ is (saddan) with a fatḥa on the sīn in both places (sadd and sadd); the majority read it with a ḍamma. The explanation of sadd was given in al-Kahf. The majority read ﴿fa-aghshaynāhum﴾ with the ghayn dotted; Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, Ibn Yaʿmar, Ikrimah, al-Nakhaʿi, Ibn Sirin, al-Ḥasan, Abu Rajaʾ, Zayd ibn ʿAli, Yazid al-Barbari, Yazid ibn al-Muhallab, Abu Ḥanifa and Ibn Miqsam read it with an ʿayn, from ʿashāʾ (night blindness), which is weakness of sight, meaning "We placed upon them a covering."

﴿And it is the same for them﴾ and the verse. Its explanation and grammatical analysis (iʿrāb) were discussed previously in the beginning of al-Baqarah.

﴿You can only warn﴾. ﴿To warn a people﴾ was mentioned earlier, but since it was decreed for them that they would not believe, until He said ﴿and it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them﴾, the warning was of no benefit, since its benefit was absent. So He said ﴿You can only warn﴾, meaning a warning that benefits whoever follows the Reminder (al-dhikr), which is the Qur'an. Qatadah said: or the admonition.

﴿And fears the Most Merciful﴾, meaning the one characterized by mercy. Though mercy may return to hope, yet with his knowledge of His mercy, he fears Him out of fear that He might deprive him of what He has bestowed upon him in the unseen (bi-l-ghayb), meaning in privacy, when the person is absent from the sight of other people. When He instilled warning in him, He gave him good news of forgiveness for what had passed; ﴿and a noble reward﴾ for the righteous deeds he had sent forth, which is Paradise.

When God, exalted is He, mentioned the messengership, which is one of the three foundations by which a person becomes a believer, He mentioned the Resurrection, which is another of the three foundations. The third is monotheism (tawḥīd). So He said ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life﴾, meaning after their death. Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥak went far in saying that the "reviving of them" means bringing them out of polytheism into faith.

﴿And We record what they have sent forth﴾, is a kinayah (allusion) for recompense, meaning: and We count it. He expressed the encompassing of His knowledge of their deeds by "writing," through which things are preserved. Zirr and Masruq read: "wa-yuktabu mā qaddamū wa-āthārahum" with the yāʾ, in the passive voice, and "what they sent forth" means deeds, and "their traces" means their steps toward the mosques. And it was said: the good and bad practices. It was also said: what they sent forth of bad deeds, and their traces are good deeds. Al-Zamakhshari said: what they sent forth of righteous deeds other than these, and what they left behind of good effect, such as knowledge they taught, a book they wrote, an endowment they established, or a building they constructed such as a mosque, a hostel, a bridge, or the like, or bad things such as a tax some oppressor imposed on the Muslims, or a coin that he introduced in which people are perplexed, or something he introduced by which people are turned away from the remembrance of God, such as melodies and frivolities. Likewise every good custom or bad custom that is followed, and similar to this is His saying, mighty and majestic, ﴿On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forth and left behind﴾ (al-Qiyamah 75:13), from his traces. End of quote. The majority read "wa-kulla shay'in" (and everything) in the accusative, as a case of ishtighāl (the verb governing a pronoun attached to the object, so the noun is put in the accusative). Abu al-Sammal read it in the nominative, as a beginning (ibtidāʾ). "The Manifest Imam" is the Preserved Tablet (al-lawḥ al-maḥfūẓ), said by Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd. Another group said it means the scrolls of deeds.

[p. 321] Surah Ya-Sin, peace be upon him. Makkiyya (Meccan), eighty-three verses.

In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿Ya-Sin.﴾ ﴿By the Qur'an, full of wisdom,﴾ ﴿indeed you are among the messengers,﴾ ﴿upon a straight path.﴾ ﴿It is a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful,﴾ ﴿that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless.﴾ ﴿The word has certainly come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles around their necks, reaching to the chins, so they are held with their heads raised.﴾ ﴿And We have placed a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, and covered them, so they do not see.﴾ ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ ﴿You can only warn one who follows the Reminder and fears the Merciful in the unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and a noble reward.﴾ ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forth and their traces, and everything We have enumerated in a clear register.﴾ ﴿And present to them a parable: the people of the town, when the messengers came to it,﴾ ﴿when We sent to them two, and they denied them, so We strengthened them with a third; and they said, "Indeed, we are messengers sent to you."﴾ ﴿They said, "You are only human beings like us, and the Merciful has revealed nothing. You are only lying."﴾ ﴿They said, "Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers to you;﴾ ﴿and our duty is only to deliver the clear message."﴾ ﴿They said, "Indeed, we see you as a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and a painful punishment from us will surely touch you."﴾ ﴿They said, "Your omen is with yourselves. Is it because you were reminded? Rather, you are a transgressing people."﴾ ﴿And there came from the farthest part of the city a man running. He said, "O my people, follow the messengers.﴾ ﴿Follow those who do not ask you for any wage, and who are guided."﴾ ﴿"And why should I not worship He who created me, and to whom you will be returned?﴾ ﴿Shall I take gods besides Him? If the Merciful intends harm for me, their intercession will avail me nothing, nor can they save me.﴾ ﴿Indeed, I would then be in clear error.﴾ ﴿Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me."﴾ ﴿It was said, "Enter Paradise." He said, "Would that my people knew﴾ ﴿of how my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honored."﴾ ﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any army from the heaven, nor were We ever to send down [one].﴾ ﴿It was but one cry, and at once they were extinguished.﴾ ﴿Alas for the servants! No messenger comes to them but that they mock him.﴾ ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, that they do not return to them?﴾ ﴿And all of them, they will surely be brought before Us.

And a sign for them is the dead earth which We have revived and brought forth from it grain, of which they eat.﴾ ﴿And We made in it gardens of palm trees and grapevines, and caused springs to gush forth from it,﴾ ﴿that they may eat of its fruit, and of what their hands produced. Will they not then be thankful?﴾ ﴿Glory be to He who created all the pairs, from what the earth grows, and from themselves, and from what they do not know.﴾ ﴿And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and at once they are in darkness.﴾ ﴿And the sun runs toward its resting place. That is the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿And the moon, We have determined for it stations until it returns like the old dry palm stalk.﴾ ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; and each is floating in an orbit.﴾ ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship,﴾ ﴿and We created for them of its like that which they ride.﴾ ﴿And if We will, We drown them, and there is no one to call for help, nor are they rescued,﴾ ﴿except as mercy from Us and enjoyment for a time.﴾ ﴿And when it is said to them, "Fear what is before you and what is behind you, that you may be shown mercy,"﴾ ﴿no sign from the signs of their Lord comes to them but that they turn away from it.﴾ ﴿And when it is said to them, "Spend from what God has provided you," those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Shall we feed one whom God would have fed if He willed? You are only in clear error."﴾ ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ ﴿They await only a single cry that will seize them while they are disputing.﴾ ﴿So they will not be able to make a bequest, nor return to their families.﴾ ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and at once they will rush from the graves to their Lord.﴾ ﴿They will say, "Woe to us! Who has raised us from our resting place? This is what the Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth."﴾ ﴿It will be but one cry, and at once they will all be brought before Us.﴾ ﴿So today no soul will be wronged in anything, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in delight,﴾ ﴿they and their spouses, in shade, reclining on couches.﴾ ﴿For them therein is fruit, and for them is whatever they call for.﴾ ﴿"Peace!" a word from a Lord, Most Merciful.﴾ (p. 322) ﴿"And stand apart today, O guilty ones.﴾ ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is a clear enemy to you,﴾ ﴿and that you should worship Me? This is a straight path.﴾ ﴿And he had already led astray a great multitude among you. Did you not then use reason?﴾ ﴿This is Hell, which you were promised.﴾ ﴿Burn therein today for what you used to disbelieve.﴾ ﴿Today We seal their mouths, and their hands speak to Us, and their feet bear witness to what they used to earn.﴾ ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes, and they would race for the path; but how could they see?﴾ ﴿And if We willed, We would have transformed them in their places, so they would not be able to proceed or return.﴾ ﴿And whomever We let live long, We reverse him in creation. Will they not then understand?﴾ ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it suitable for him. It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an,﴾ ﴿to warn whoever is alive, and that the word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿Do they not see that We have created for them, from what Our hands have made, cattle, and they are their owners?﴾ ﴿And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat.﴾ ﴿And for them in them are benefits and drinks. Will they not then be thankful?﴾ ﴿And they have taken gods besides God, hoping they might be helped.﴾ ﴿They cannot help them, and they are a mobilized host for them.﴾ ﴿So do not let their saying grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they reveal.﴾ ﴿Has not man seen that We created him from a drop, and then he is an open adversary?﴾ ﴿And he has struck for Us a parable and forgotten his creation. He said, "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ ﴿Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knower of all creation.﴾ ﴿He who made for you from the green tree fire, and then you kindle from it."﴾ ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Yes, indeed; He is the All-Creating, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ ﴿So glory be to He in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned.﴾

Qamaḥa al-ba'īru ra'sahu (قَمَحَ البَعِيرُ رَأْسَهُ): he raised his head, after drinking water; the discussion of it will come in full. Al-ʿurjūn (العُرْجُونُ): the stalk of the date cluster, from between the stem to its point of origin on the palm tree. Al-Zajjaj said: it is fuʿlūn, from al-inʿirāj, which is bending. Al-jadath (الجَدَثُ): the grave. It is also heard as jadaf, with the thāʾ replaced by fāʾ, as they said fumm for thumm; and as they replaced fāʾ with thāʾ, they said maʿthūr for maʿfūr. It is a kind of truffle. Al-maskh (المَسْخُ): transformation from one form into a hideous form. Al-ramīm (الرَّمِيمُ): decayed and crumbling.

* *

﴿Ya-Sin.﴾ ﴿By the Qur'an, full of wisdom,﴾ ﴿indeed you are among the messengers,﴾ ﴿upon a straight path.﴾ ﴿It is a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful,﴾ ﴿that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless.﴾ ﴿The word has certainly come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles around their necks, reaching to the chins, so they are held with their heads raised.﴾ ﴿And We have placed a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, and covered them, so they do not see.﴾ ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ ﴿You can only warn one who follows the Reminder and fears the Merciful in the unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and a noble reward.﴾ ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forth and their traces, and everything We have enumerated in a clear register.﴾.

This surah is Meccan, except that a group claimed that His words ﴿and We record what they have sent forth﴾ and "their traces" were revealed concerning the Banu Salama of the Ansar, when they wanted to leave their homes and move to be near the Mosque of the Messenger; but this claim is not correct. It is also said: except His words ﴿And when it is said to them, "Spend from what God has provided you"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 47] and the verse that follows.

The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. Ibn Jubayr said here: it is one of the names of Muhammad (ﷺ), and its evidence is ﴿indeed you are among the messengers﴾. Sayyid al-Hamawi said:

"O soul, do not purify yourself with love, striving for affection, except for the family of Yasin."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: its meaning is "O human" in Ethiopian (Habashi). And from him: it is in the dialect of Tayy, for they say īsān meaning insān, and they pluralize it as ayāsīn; so this is from it. Another group said: yā is a vocative particle, and the sīn stands in place of insān, from which a letter was removed and it was placed in its stead. Al-Zamakhshari said: if it is true that its meaning is "O human" in the dialect of Tayy, then its basis is to be ya-unaysīn, and the calling was so frequent on their tongues that they limited it to a part of it, as they said in the oath: mu-llāh and ayman-llāh. End of quote. What is reported from the Arabs in the diminutive of insān is unaysiyān, with a yāʾ followed by an alif, which indicates that its root is unaysān, because diminution returns things to their roots; and we do not know that they said its diminutive as unaysīn. And even on the assumption that it is a remnant of unaysīn, that is not permissible, neither being built on a ḍamma nor remaining pausal; because it is a vocative addressed directly, and also it is not permissible because it is a diminutive, and that is impermissible with regard to the prophethood. His saying "as they said in the oath mu-llāh and ayman-llāh" is one view. Among the grammarians there are those who say that mu is a particle of oath and is not a remnant of ayman.

It was read with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, with its pure imāla (inclination), and between the two pronunciations. The majority read with a sukūn on the nūn, assimilated into the wāw. Among the seven: al-Kisa'i, Abu Bakr, Warsh, and Ibn ʿAmir read it with clear pronunciation, while the rest of the seven read it as assimilated. Ibn Abi Ishaq and ʿIsa read with a fatḥa on the nūn. Qatada said: Yasin is an oath. Abu Hatim said: the analogy of this view is a fatḥa on the nūn, as you say: "Allāh, I will certainly do such-and-such." Al-Zajjaj said: a naṣb, as if he said: "Recite Yasin," and this is according to Sibawayh's view that it is a name for the surah. Al-Kalbi read with a ḍamma on the nūn, and said it is in the dialect of Tayy: "O human." Al-Sammak and Ibn Abi Ishaq also read with a kasra. It was said: the vowel is because of the meeting of two sukūns; the fatḥa is sought for lightness, the ḍamma like ḥaythu, and the kasra is on the basis of their meeting. If it is said that it is an oath, it may be in the naṣb position according to Abu Hatim's view, the rafʿ as a mubtada' (subject), like "the trust of God, I will surely stand," and the jarr by implying a particle of jarr, which is permissible according to the Kufans. (Al-Ḥakīm): either it is faʿīl in the sense of mufʿal, as you say: "I tied the honey, so it is ʿaqīd," meaning maʿqūd; or it is for emphasis from ḥākim; or it is in the sense of cause, that is, possessing wisdom.

﴿Upon a straight path﴾ is a second predicate, or it is in the position of a circumstantial clause from him, peace be upon him, or from "the messengers," or it is related to "the messengers." The straight path is the law of Islam.

Talha, al-Ashhab and ʿIsa read, according to the varying reports from them, tanzīla with a naṣb as a verbal noun; Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read tanzīla with a naṣb as a verbal noun; the rest of the seven, Abu Bakr, Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, al-Hasan, al-Aʿraj, and al-Aʿmash read it with a rafʿ as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: it is a revelation. Abu Ḥaywa, al-Yazidi, and al-Qursi from Abu Jaʿfar and Shayba read it with a jarr, either as an apposition to "the Qur'an," or as a description by a verbal noun. (Li-tundhira) is related to tanzīl or to arsalnā implied.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 36, verses 1–20 (part 2 of 2):

﴿What their fathers were warned of﴾. Ikrimah said: "mā" means "alladhī" (the one that), i.e., "the thing that their fathers were warned of, of the punishment." Then "mā" is the second object, as in His saying ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾ (al-Naba 78:40). Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: "It is also possible that mā is a verbal noun (maṣdariyyah), meaning ﴿what their fathers were warned﴾, and the fathers in this case are the earliest of the descendants of Ismaʿil, among whom warning had existed." And "fa-hum" (so they) according to this interpretation means "fa-innahum" (for they). The fāʾ is used to separate one clause from another clause that stands as a relative clause (ṣilah), so it connects to His saying ﴿Indeed, you are among the messengers﴾. The phrase "to warn" (li-tundhira) is like when you say: "I sent you to so-and-so to warn him, for he is heedless, or rather he is heedless." Qatadah said: "mā" is a negation, meaning that their fathers were not warned. In this case, "their fathers" are the nearer ones among them, and "mā undhira" is in the position of a qualifier, meaning "whose fathers were not warned." "Fa-hum ghafilūn" (so they are heedless) is connected to the negation, meaning: they were not warned, so they are heedless, since their not being warned is the cause of their heedlessness. By considering the fathers in terms of their antiquity and nearness, the contradiction between warning and its negation disappears.

﴿Indeed, the word has come into effect against most of them﴾. The well-known view is that the word is ﴿I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together﴾ (Hud 11:119). It was also said: it means that the necessity of punishment was already decreed in His knowledge. And it was said: "the word" (al-qawl) [p. 324] is what God said through the tongue of the messengers, concerning monotheism and other matters, and its proof became clear; so most of them do not believe after that. The apparent meaning of His saying ﴿Indeed, We have placed shackles upon their necks﴾ and what follows is that it is literal, not metaphorical (istiʿārah, metaphor). When God, exalted is He, stated that they do not believe, He then informed about some of their conditions in the Hereafter when they enter the Fire. Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: "His saying ﴿So We covered them, and they cannot see﴾ weakens this view, because the sight of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection is sharp, seeing the ugliness of their state." End of quote. But this does not weaken it. Do you not see His saying ﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind﴾ (al-Isra 17:97), and His saying ﴿He will say: My Lord, why have You gathered me blind?﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:125)? Or His saying ﴿So your sight today is sharp﴾ (Qaf 50:22) may be a kinayah (metonymy, allusion) for his grasp of what he is coming to, as if he sees it. The majority said: that is a metaphor. Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Ishaq said: it is a metaphor for the state of the disbelievers who intended harm to the Messenger; God made this an example for them in restraining them from him and preventing them from harming him when they plotted against him. Al-Ḍaḥḥak and al-Farrāʾ said: it is a metaphor for their withholding from spending in the way of God, as He said ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾ (al-Isra 17:29). Ikrimah said: it was revealed when Abu Jahl intended to strike him with a great stone, and in other such occasions, but God prevented him. This is close to the view of Ibn ʿAbbas. It is narrated that "Abu Jahl carried a stone to throw at the Prophet ﷺ while he was praying, and his hands were bent up to his neck, so that he returned to his companions with the stone stuck in his hand. They could not free it except with great effort. Then he took another stone, but when he approached the Messenger, God blinded his sight so he did not see him. He returned to his companions and could not see them until they called out to him." So the shackle becoming a metaphor refers to the restraint of Abu Jahl and others in this story. And since Abu Jahl's companions were content with what he intended to do, this was attributed to a group. Another group said: it is a metaphor for God's preventing them from faith and His placing a barrier between them and it. Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: this is the most preferred of the views, because when God mentioned that they do not believe, due to what had been decreed for them from eternity, He followed this with making for them a restraint and an encompassing wretchedness in which their state is like that of those who are shackled. End of quote. Al-Zamakhshari said: it is an image (tamthīl) of their insistence upon disbelief, and that there is no way to their claim of [being guided], as He made them like the shackled, head-raised (muqmaḥūn), in that they do not turn toward the truth, nor bend their necks toward it, nor lower their heads to it; and like those confined between two barriers, who see neither what is before them nor what is behind them, in that they have no reflection and do not see, meaning they are blind to considering the signs of God, exalted is He. End of quote. In his words there is a hidden trace of Muʿtazilism (dasīsat al-iʿtizāl). Do you not see that the statement of the People of the Sunnah (ahl al-sunnah, the orthodox majority) is "a metaphor for God's preventing them from faith," while al-Zamakhshari's statement is "an image of their insistence," and he attributes the actions that he counts to them and not to God? The ghull (shackle) is that which surrounds the neck, for the sake of rebuke, constriction, punishment, and captivity. With the neck, both hands or one hand [are bound], for the sake of explanation (taʿlīl). The apparent reference of the pronoun in "fa-hiya" (so they are) is to the shackles, because they are the ones mentioned and spoken of. Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: they are broad, reaching the chin with their edges, and the chin is the junction of the two jaws, so the shackled man is compelled to raise his face toward the sky, and that is iqmāḥ (raising the head with lowered gaze), which is close to the meaning of being held with a halter in appearance. Al-Zamakhshari said: the shackles, the origin of which is "up to the chins," are fastened to them. That is because the collar of the shackle, which is around the neck of the shackled one, has at the meeting of its two ends under the chin a ring in which the head of the post sits, passing through the ring up to the chin, so it does not let him lower his head or lay his nape down, so he remains always raising his head. End of quote. Al-Farrāʾ said: qamḥ is that in which one lowers his gaze after raising his head. Al-Zajjaj said something similar, saying: it is said "qamaḥa al-baʿīr raʾsahu ʿan rayy" (the camel raised its head away from water) and "qamaḥa" (it did so). Abu ʿUbayda said: qamaḥa qumūḥan: he raised his head from the pool without drinking, and the plural is qiṣāḥ (camels that raise their heads). From this is the saying of Bishr, describing the death of one of them so that they would bury him:

"We sit around its sides, lowering our gaze like camels with raised heads (qiṣāḥ)."

Al-Layth said: it is the raising of the camel's head when it drinks bad water, then it returns. Al-Zajjaj said: the two months of the winter (al-kānūnayn) are called "shahrā qimāḥ" because when camels come to water they raise their heads because of its extreme coldness. Abu Zayd recited the verse of al-Hudhali:

"A youth, the son of the mighty, when we pass the winter, and provisions are loved in the two months of qimāḥ."

He narrated it with a ḍamma on the qāf, and Ibn al-Sikkit with a kasra, and both are dialects. The two were called "the two months of qimāḥ" because every creature with a liver dislikes drinking water in them. Al-Ḥasan said: al-qāmiḥ is one who raises his gaze toward the place of his foot. Mujahid said: the one raising the head, the one placing his hand over his mouth. Al-Ṭabarī said: the pronoun in "fa-hiya" refers to the hands, even though no mention of them preceded, because its place is clear from the meaning, since the shackle is only on the neck with the two hands, which is why the shackle was named "jāmiʿah" (gatherer), for it gathers the hand and the neck. ʿAli, may God honor his face, saw people raising their heads, so he placed his hands under his jaws and pressed them and raised his head. Al-Zamakhshari said: he made the qimāḥ the result of His saying ﴿so they are up to the chins﴾. If the pronoun referred to the hands, the sense of causation in the qimāḥ would not be apparent; and this placement of a pronoun involves a kind of contrivance and abandoning of the apparent meaning, which the meaning itself calls for, toward falsehood, which turns away from the clear truth toward a confused falsehood. End of quote.

The reading of ʿAbd Allah, Ikrimah, al-Nakhaʿi, Ibn Wathhab, Talha, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Ibn Kathir and Ḥafṣ is (saddan) with a fatḥa on the sīn in both places (sadd and sadd); the majority read it with a ḍamma. The explanation of sadd was given in al-Kahf. The majority read ﴿fa-aghshaynāhum﴾ with the ghayn dotted; Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, Ibn Yaʿmar, Ikrimah, al-Nakhaʿi, Ibn Sirin, al-Ḥasan, Abu Rajaʾ, Zayd ibn ʿAli, Yazid al-Barbari, Yazid ibn al-Muhallab, Abu Ḥanifa and Ibn Miqsam read it with an ʿayn, from ʿashāʾ (night blindness), which is weakness of sight, meaning "We placed upon them a covering."

﴿And it is the same for them﴾ and the verse. Its explanation and grammatical analysis (iʿrāb) were discussed previously in the beginning of al-Baqarah.

﴿You can only warn﴾. ﴿To warn a people﴾ was mentioned earlier, but since it was decreed for them that they would not believe, until He said ﴿and it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them﴾, the warning was of no benefit, since its benefit was absent. So He said ﴿You can only warn﴾, meaning a warning that benefits whoever follows the Reminder (al-dhikr), which is the Qur'an. Qatadah said: or the admonition.

﴿And fears the Most Merciful﴾, meaning the one characterized by mercy. Though mercy may return to hope, yet with his knowledge of His mercy, he fears Him out of fear that He might deprive him of what He has bestowed upon him in the unseen (bi-l-ghayb), meaning in privacy, when the person is absent from the sight of other people. When He instilled warning in him, He gave him good news of forgiveness for what had passed; ﴿and a noble reward﴾ for the righteous deeds he had sent forth, which is Paradise.

When God, exalted is He, mentioned the messengership, which is one of the three foundations by which a person becomes a believer, He mentioned the Resurrection, which is another of the three foundations. The third is monotheism (tawḥīd). So He said ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life﴾, meaning after their death. Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥak went far in saying that the "reviving of them" means bringing them out of polytheism into faith.

﴿And We record what they have sent forth﴾, is a kinayah (allusion) for recompense, meaning: and We count it. He expressed the encompassing of His knowledge of their deeds by "writing," through which things are preserved. Zirr and Masruq read: "wa-yuktabu mā qaddamū wa-āthārahum" with the yāʾ, in the passive voice, and "what they sent forth" means deeds, and "their traces" means their steps toward the mosques. And it was said: the good and bad practices. It was also said: what they sent forth of bad deeds, and their traces are good deeds. Al-Zamakhshari said: what they sent forth of righteous deeds other than these, and what they left behind of good effect, such as knowledge they taught, a book they wrote, an endowment they established, or a building they constructed such as a mosque, a hostel, a bridge, or the like, or bad things such as a tax some oppressor imposed on the Muslims, or a coin that he introduced in which people are perplexed, or something he introduced by which people are turned away from the remembrance of God, such as melodies and frivolities. Likewise every good custom or bad custom that is followed, and similar to this is His saying, mighty and majestic, ﴿On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forth and left behind﴾ (al-Qiyamah 75:13), from his traces. End of quote. The majority read "wa-kulla shay'in" (and everything) in the accusative, as a case of ishtighāl (the verb governing a pronoun attached to the object, so the noun is put in the accusative). Abu al-Sammal read it in the nominative, as a beginning (ibtidāʾ). "The Manifest Imam" is the Preserved Tablet (al-lawḥ al-maḥfūẓ), said by Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd. Another group said it means the scrolls of deeds.

[p. 321] Surah Ya-Sin, peace be upon him. Makkiyya (Meccan), eighty-three verses.

In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿Ya-Sin.﴾ ﴿By the Qur'an, full of wisdom,﴾ ﴿indeed you are among the messengers,﴾ ﴿upon a straight path.﴾ ﴿It is a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful,﴾ ﴿that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless.﴾ ﴿The word has certainly come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles around their necks, reaching to the chins, so they are held with their heads raised.﴾ ﴿And We have placed a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, and covered them, so they do not see.﴾ ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ ﴿You can only warn one who follows the Reminder and fears the Merciful in the unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and a noble reward.﴾ ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forth and their traces, and everything We have enumerated in a clear register.﴾ ﴿And present to them a parable: the people of the town, when the messengers came to it,﴾ ﴿when We sent to them two, and they denied them, so We strengthened them with a third; and they said, "Indeed, we are messengers sent to you."﴾ ﴿They said, "You are only human beings like us, and the Merciful has revealed nothing. You are only lying."﴾ ﴿They said, "Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers to you;﴾ ﴿and our duty is only to deliver the clear message."﴾ ﴿They said, "Indeed, we see you as a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and a painful punishment from us will surely touch you."﴾ ﴿They said, "Your omen is with yourselves. Is it because you were reminded? Rather, you are a transgressing people."﴾ ﴿And there came from the farthest part of the city a man running. He said, "O my people, follow the messengers.﴾ ﴿Follow those who do not ask you for any wage, and who are guided."﴾ ﴿"And why should I not worship He who created me, and to whom you will be returned?﴾ ﴿Shall I take gods besides Him? If the Merciful intends harm for me, their intercession will avail me nothing, nor can they save me.﴾ ﴿Indeed, I would then be in clear error.﴾ ﴿Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me."﴾ ﴿It was said, "Enter Paradise." He said, "Would that my people knew﴾ ﴿of how my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honored."﴾ ﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any army from the heaven, nor were We ever to send down [one].﴾ ﴿It was but one cry, and at once they were extinguished.﴾ ﴿Alas for the servants! No messenger comes to them but that they mock him.﴾ ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, that they do not return to them?﴾ ﴿And all of them, they will surely be brought before Us.

And a sign for them is the dead earth which We have revived and brought forth from it grain, of which they eat.﴾ ﴿And We made in it gardens of palm trees and grapevines, and caused springs to gush forth from it,﴾ ﴿that they may eat of its fruit, and of what their hands produced. Will they not then be thankful?﴾ ﴿Glory be to He who created all the pairs, from what the earth grows, and from themselves, and from what they do not know.﴾ ﴿And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and at once they are in darkness.﴾ ﴿And the sun runs toward its resting place. That is the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿And the moon, We have determined for it stations until it returns like the old dry palm stalk.﴾ ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; and each is floating in an orbit.﴾ ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship,﴾ ﴿and We created for them of its like that which they ride.﴾ ﴿And if We will, We drown them, and there is no one to call for help, nor are they rescued,﴾ ﴿except as mercy from Us and enjoyment for a time.﴾ ﴿And when it is said to them, "Fear what is before you and what is behind you, that you may be shown mercy,"﴾ ﴿no sign from the signs of their Lord comes to them but that they turn away from it.﴾ ﴿And when it is said to them, "Spend from what God has provided you," those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Shall we feed one whom God would have fed if He willed? You are only in clear error."﴾ ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ ﴿They await only a single cry that will seize them while they are disputing.﴾ ﴿So they will not be able to make a bequest, nor return to their families.﴾ ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and at once they will rush from the graves to their Lord.﴾ ﴿They will say, "Woe to us! Who has raised us from our resting place? This is what the Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth."﴾ ﴿It will be but one cry, and at once they will all be brought before Us.﴾ ﴿So today no soul will be wronged in anything, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in delight,﴾ ﴿they and their spouses, in shade, reclining on couches.﴾ ﴿For them therein is fruit, and for them is whatever they call for.﴾ ﴿"Peace!" a word from a Lord, Most Merciful.﴾ (p. 322) ﴿"And stand apart today, O guilty ones.﴾ ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is a clear enemy to you,﴾ ﴿and that you should worship Me? This is a straight path.﴾ ﴿And he had already led astray a great multitude among you. Did you not then use reason?﴾ ﴿This is Hell, which you were promised.﴾ ﴿Burn therein today for what you used to disbelieve.﴾ ﴿Today We seal their mouths, and their hands speak to Us, and their feet bear witness to what they used to earn.﴾ ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes, and they would race for the path; but how could they see?﴾ ﴿And if We willed, We would have transformed them in their places, so they would not be able to proceed or return.﴾ ﴿And whomever We let live long, We reverse him in creation. Will they not then understand?﴾ ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it suitable for him. It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an,﴾ ﴿to warn whoever is alive, and that the word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿Do they not see that We have created for them, from what Our hands have made, cattle, and they are their owners?﴾ ﴿And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat.﴾ ﴿And for them in them are benefits and drinks. Will they not then be thankful?﴾ ﴿And they have taken gods besides God, hoping they might be helped.﴾ ﴿They cannot help them, and they are a mobilized host for them.﴾ ﴿So do not let their saying grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they reveal.﴾ ﴿Has not man seen that We created him from a drop, and then he is an open adversary?﴾ ﴿And he has struck for Us a parable and forgotten his creation. He said, "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ ﴿Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knower of all creation.﴾ ﴿He who made for you from the green tree fire, and then you kindle from it."﴾ ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Yes, indeed; He is the All-Creating, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ ﴿So glory be to He in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned.﴾

Qamaḥa al-ba'īru ra'sahu (قَمَحَ البَعِيرُ رَأْسَهُ): he raised his head, after drinking water; the discussion of it will come in full. Al-ʿurjūn (العُرْجُونُ): the stalk of the date cluster, from between the stem to its point of origin on the palm tree. Al-Zajjaj said: it is fuʿlūn, from al-inʿirāj, which is bending. Al-jadath (الجَدَثُ): the grave. It is also heard as jadaf, with the thāʾ replaced by fāʾ, as they said fumm for thumm; and as they replaced fāʾ with thāʾ, they said maʿthūr for maʿfūr. It is a kind of truffle. Al-maskh (المَسْخُ): transformation from one form into a hideous form. Al-ramīm (الرَّمِيمُ): decayed and crumbling.

* *

﴿Ya-Sin.﴾ ﴿By the Qur'an, full of wisdom,﴾ ﴿indeed you are among the messengers,﴾ ﴿upon a straight path.﴾ ﴿It is a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful,﴾ ﴿that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless.﴾ ﴿The word has certainly come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles around their necks, reaching to the chins, so they are held with their heads raised.﴾ ﴿And We have placed a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, and covered them, so they do not see.﴾ ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ ﴿You can only warn one who follows the Reminder and fears the Merciful in the unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and a noble reward.﴾ ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forth and their traces, and everything We have enumerated in a clear register.﴾.

This surah is Meccan, except that a group claimed that His words ﴿and We record what they have sent forth﴾ and "their traces" were revealed concerning the Banu Salama of the Ansar, when they wanted to leave their homes and move to be near the Mosque of the Messenger; but this claim is not correct. It is also said: except His words ﴿And when it is said to them, "Spend from what God has provided you"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 47] and the verse that follows.

The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. Ibn Jubayr said here: it is one of the names of Muhammad (ﷺ), and its evidence is ﴿indeed you are among the messengers﴾. Sayyid al-Hamawi said:

"O soul, do not purify yourself with love, striving for affection, except for the family of Yasin."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: its meaning is "O human" in Ethiopian (Habashi). And from him: it is in the dialect of Tayy, for they say īsān meaning insān, and they pluralize it as ayāsīn; so this is from it. Another group said: yā is a vocative particle, and the sīn stands in place of insān, from which a letter was removed and it was placed in its stead. Al-Zamakhshari said: if it is true that its meaning is "O human" in the dialect of Tayy, then its basis is to be ya-unaysīn, and the calling was so frequent on their tongues that they limited it to a part of it, as they said in the oath: mu-llāh and ayman-llāh. End of quote. What is reported from the Arabs in the diminutive of insān is unaysiyān, with a yāʾ followed by an alif, which indicates that its root is unaysān, because diminution returns things to their roots; and we do not know that they said its diminutive as unaysīn. And even on the assumption that it is a remnant of unaysīn, that is not permissible, neither being built on a ḍamma nor remaining pausal; because it is a vocative addressed directly, and also it is not permissible because it is a diminutive, and that is impermissible with regard to the prophethood. His saying "as they said in the oath mu-llāh and ayman-llāh" is one view. Among the grammarians there are those who say that mu is a particle of oath and is not a remnant of ayman.

It was read with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, with its pure imāla (inclination), and between the two pronunciations. The majority read with a sukūn on the nūn, assimilated into the wāw. Among the seven: al-Kisa'i, Abu Bakr, Warsh, and Ibn ʿAmir read it with clear pronunciation, while the rest of the seven read it as assimilated. Ibn Abi Ishaq and ʿIsa read with a fatḥa on the nūn. Qatada said: Yasin is an oath. Abu Hatim said: the analogy of this view is a fatḥa on the nūn, as you say: "Allāh, I will certainly do such-and-such." Al-Zajjaj said: a naṣb, as if he said: "Recite Yasin," and this is according to Sibawayh's view that it is a name for the surah. Al-Kalbi read with a ḍamma on the nūn, and said it is in the dialect of Tayy: "O human." Al-Sammak and Ibn Abi Ishaq also read with a kasra. It was said: the vowel is because of the meeting of two sukūns; the fatḥa is sought for lightness, the ḍamma like ḥaythu, and the kasra is on the basis of their meeting. If it is said that it is an oath, it may be in the naṣb position according to Abu Hatim's view, the rafʿ as a mubtada' (subject), like "the trust of God, I will surely stand," and the jarr by implying a particle of jarr, which is permissible according to the Kufans. (Al-Ḥakīm): either it is faʿīl in the sense of mufʿal, as you say: "I tied the honey, so it is ʿaqīd," meaning maʿqūd; or it is for emphasis from ḥākim; or it is in the sense of cause, that is, possessing wisdom.

﴿Upon a straight path﴾ is a second predicate, or it is in the position of a circumstantial clause from him, peace be upon him, or from "the messengers," or it is related to "the messengers." The straight path is the law of Islam.

Talha, al-Ashhab and ʿIsa read, according to the varying reports from them, tanzīla with a naṣb as a verbal noun; Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read tanzīla with a naṣb as a verbal noun; the rest of the seven, Abu Bakr, Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, al-Hasan, al-Aʿraj, and al-Aʿmash read it with a rafʿ as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: it is a revelation. Abu Ḥaywa, al-Yazidi, and al-Qursi from Abu Jaʿfar and Shayba read it with a jarr, either as an apposition to "the Qur'an," or as a description by a verbal noun. (Li-tundhira) is related to tanzīl or to arsalnā implied.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 36, verses 1–20 (part 2 of 2):

﴿What their fathers were warned of﴾. Ikrimah said: "mā" means "alladhī" (the one that), i.e., "the thing that their fathers were warned of, of the punishment." Then "mā" is the second object, as in His saying ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾ (al-Naba 78:40). Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: "It is also possible that mā is a verbal noun (maṣdariyyah), meaning ﴿what their fathers were warned﴾, and the fathers in this case are the earliest of the descendants of Ismaʿil, among whom warning had existed." And "fa-hum" (so they) according to this interpretation means "fa-innahum" (for they). The fāʾ is used to separate one clause from another clause that stands as a relative clause (ṣilah), so it connects to His saying ﴿Indeed, you are among the messengers﴾. The phrase "to warn" (li-tundhira) is like when you say: "I sent you to so-and-so to warn him, for he is heedless, or rather he is heedless." Qatadah said: "mā" is a negation, meaning that their fathers were not warned. In this case, "their fathers" are the nearer ones among them, and "mā undhira" is in the position of a qualifier, meaning "whose fathers were not warned." "Fa-hum ghafilūn" (so they are heedless) is connected to the negation, meaning: they were not warned, so they are heedless, since their not being warned is the cause of their heedlessness. By considering the fathers in terms of their antiquity and nearness, the contradiction between warning and its negation disappears.

﴿Indeed, the word has come into effect against most of them﴾. The well-known view is that the word is ﴿I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together﴾ (Hud 11:119). It was also said: it means that the necessity of punishment was already decreed in His knowledge. And it was said: "the word" (al-qawl) [p. 324] is what God said through the tongue of the messengers, concerning monotheism and other matters, and its proof became clear; so most of them do not believe after that. The apparent meaning of His saying ﴿Indeed, We have placed shackles upon their necks﴾ and what follows is that it is literal, not metaphorical (istiʿārah, metaphor). When God, exalted is He, stated that they do not believe, He then informed about some of their conditions in the Hereafter when they enter the Fire. Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: "His saying ﴿So We covered them, and they cannot see﴾ weakens this view, because the sight of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection is sharp, seeing the ugliness of their state." End of quote. But this does not weaken it. Do you not see His saying ﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind﴾ (al-Isra 17:97), and His saying ﴿He will say: My Lord, why have You gathered me blind?﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:125)? Or His saying ﴿So your sight today is sharp﴾ (Qaf 50:22) may be a kinayah (metonymy, allusion) for his grasp of what he is coming to, as if he sees it. The majority said: that is a metaphor. Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Ishaq said: it is a metaphor for the state of the disbelievers who intended harm to the Messenger; God made this an example for them in restraining them from him and preventing them from harming him when they plotted against him. Al-Ḍaḥḥak and al-Farrāʾ said: it is a metaphor for their withholding from spending in the way of God, as He said ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾ (al-Isra 17:29). Ikrimah said: it was revealed when Abu Jahl intended to strike him with a great stone, and in other such occasions, but God prevented him. This is close to the view of Ibn ʿAbbas. It is narrated that "Abu Jahl carried a stone to throw at the Prophet ﷺ while he was praying, and his hands were bent up to his neck, so that he returned to his companions with the stone stuck in his hand. They could not free it except with great effort. Then he took another stone, but when he approached the Messenger, God blinded his sight so he did not see him. He returned to his companions and could not see them until they called out to him." So the shackle becoming a metaphor refers to the restraint of Abu Jahl and others in this story. And since Abu Jahl's companions were content with what he intended to do, this was attributed to a group. Another group said: it is a metaphor for God's preventing them from faith and His placing a barrier between them and it. Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: this is the most preferred of the views, because when God mentioned that they do not believe, due to what had been decreed for them from eternity, He followed this with making for them a restraint and an encompassing wretchedness in which their state is like that of those who are shackled. End of quote. Al-Zamakhshari said: it is an image (tamthīl) of their insistence upon disbelief, and that there is no way to their claim of [being guided], as He made them like the shackled, head-raised (muqmaḥūn), in that they do not turn toward the truth, nor bend their necks toward it, nor lower their heads to it; and like those confined between two barriers, who see neither what is before them nor what is behind them, in that they have no reflection and do not see, meaning they are blind to considering the signs of God, exalted is He. End of quote. In his words there is a hidden trace of Muʿtazilism (dasīsat al-iʿtizāl). Do you not see that the statement of the People of the Sunnah (ahl al-sunnah, the orthodox majority) is "a metaphor for God's preventing them from faith," while al-Zamakhshari's statement is "an image of their insistence," and he attributes the actions that he counts to them and not to God? The ghull (shackle) is that which surrounds the neck, for the sake of rebuke, constriction, punishment, and captivity. With the neck, both hands or one hand [are bound], for the sake of explanation (taʿlīl). The apparent reference of the pronoun in "fa-hiya" (so they are) is to the shackles, because they are the ones mentioned and spoken of. Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: they are broad, reaching the chin with their edges, and the chin is the junction of the two jaws, so the shackled man is compelled to raise his face toward the sky, and that is iqmāḥ (raising the head with lowered gaze), which is close to the meaning of being held with a halter in appearance. Al-Zamakhshari said: the shackles, the origin of which is "up to the chins," are fastened to them. That is because the collar of the shackle, which is around the neck of the shackled one, has at the meeting of its two ends under the chin a ring in which the head of the post sits, passing through the ring up to the chin, so it does not let him lower his head or lay his nape down, so he remains always raising his head. End of quote. Al-Farrāʾ said: qamḥ is that in which one lowers his gaze after raising his head. Al-Zajjaj said something similar, saying: it is said "qamaḥa al-baʿīr raʾsahu ʿan rayy" (the camel raised its head away from water) and "qamaḥa" (it did so). Abu ʿUbayda said: qamaḥa qumūḥan: he raised his head from the pool without drinking, and the plural is qiṣāḥ (camels that raise their heads). From this is the saying of Bishr, describing the death of one of them so that they would bury him:

"We sit around its sides, lowering our gaze like camels with raised heads (qiṣāḥ)."

Al-Layth said: it is the raising of the camel's head when it drinks bad water, then it returns. Al-Zajjaj said: the two months of the winter (al-kānūnayn) are called "shahrā qimāḥ" because when camels come to water they raise their heads because of its extreme coldness. Abu Zayd recited the verse of al-Hudhali:

"A youth, the son of the mighty, when we pass the winter, and provisions are loved in the two months of qimāḥ."

He narrated it with a ḍamma on the qāf, and Ibn al-Sikkit with a kasra, and both are dialects. The two were called "the two months of qimāḥ" because every creature with a liver dislikes drinking water in them. Al-Ḥasan said: al-qāmiḥ is one who raises his gaze toward the place of his foot. Mujahid said: the one raising the head, the one placing his hand over his mouth. Al-Ṭabarī said: the pronoun in "fa-hiya" refers to the hands, even though no mention of them preceded, because its place is clear from the meaning, since the shackle is only on the neck with the two hands, which is why the shackle was named "jāmiʿah" (gatherer), for it gathers the hand and the neck. ʿAli, may God honor his face, saw people raising their heads, so he placed his hands under his jaws and pressed them and raised his head. Al-Zamakhshari said: he made the qimāḥ the result of His saying ﴿so they are up to the chins﴾. If the pronoun referred to the hands, the sense of causation in the qimāḥ would not be apparent; and this placement of a pronoun involves a kind of contrivance and abandoning of the apparent meaning, which the meaning itself calls for, toward falsehood, which turns away from the clear truth toward a confused falsehood. End of quote.

The reading of ʿAbd Allah, Ikrimah, al-Nakhaʿi, Ibn Wathhab, Talha, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Ibn Kathir and Ḥafṣ is (saddan) with a fatḥa on the sīn in both places (sadd and sadd); the majority read it with a ḍamma. The explanation of sadd was given in al-Kahf. The majority read ﴿fa-aghshaynāhum﴾ with the ghayn dotted; Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, Ibn Yaʿmar, Ikrimah, al-Nakhaʿi, Ibn Sirin, al-Ḥasan, Abu Rajaʾ, Zayd ibn ʿAli, Yazid al-Barbari, Yazid ibn al-Muhallab, Abu Ḥanifa and Ibn Miqsam read it with an ʿayn, from ʿashāʾ (night blindness), which is weakness of sight, meaning "We placed upon them a covering."

﴿And it is the same for them﴾ and the verse. Its explanation and grammatical analysis (iʿrāb) were discussed previously in the beginning of al-Baqarah.

﴿You can only warn﴾. ﴿To warn a people﴾ was mentioned earlier, but since it was decreed for them that they would not believe, until He said ﴿and it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them﴾, the warning was of no benefit, since its benefit was absent. So He said ﴿You can only warn﴾, meaning a warning that benefits whoever follows the Reminder (al-dhikr), which is the Qur'an. Qatadah said: or the admonition.

﴿And fears the Most Merciful﴾, meaning the one characterized by mercy. Though mercy may return to hope, yet with his knowledge of His mercy, he fears Him out of fear that He might deprive him of what He has bestowed upon him in the unseen (bi-l-ghayb), meaning in privacy, when the person is absent from the sight of other people. When He instilled warning in him, He gave him good news of forgiveness for what had passed; ﴿and a noble reward﴾ for the righteous deeds he had sent forth, which is Paradise.

When God, exalted is He, mentioned the messengership, which is one of the three foundations by which a person becomes a believer, He mentioned the Resurrection, which is another of the three foundations. The third is monotheism (tawḥīd). So He said ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life﴾, meaning after their death. Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥak went far in saying that the "reviving of them" means bringing them out of polytheism into faith.

﴿And We record what they have sent forth﴾, is a kinayah (allusion) for recompense, meaning: and We count it. He expressed the encompassing of His knowledge of their deeds by "writing," through which things are preserved. Zirr and Masruq read: "wa-yuktabu mā qaddamū wa-āthārahum" with the yāʾ, in the passive voice, and "what they sent forth" means deeds, and "their traces" means their steps toward the mosques. And it was said: the good and bad practices. It was also said: what they sent forth of bad deeds, and their traces are good deeds. Al-Zamakhshari said: what they sent forth of righteous deeds other than these, and what they left behind of good effect, such as knowledge they taught, a book they wrote, an endowment they established, or a building they constructed such as a mosque, a hostel, a bridge, or the like, or bad things such as a tax some oppressor imposed on the Muslims, or a coin that he introduced in which people are perplexed, or something he introduced by which people are turned away from the remembrance of God, such as melodies and frivolities. Likewise every good custom or bad custom that is followed, and similar to this is His saying, mighty and majestic, ﴿On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forth and left behind﴾ (al-Qiyamah 75:13), from his traces. End of quote. The majority read "wa-kulla shay'in" (and everything) in the accusative, as a case of ishtighāl (the verb governing a pronoun attached to the object, so the noun is put in the accusative). Abu al-Sammal read it in the nominative, as a beginning (ibtidāʾ). "The Manifest Imam" is the Preserved Tablet (al-lawḥ al-maḥfūẓ), said by Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd. Another group said it means the scrolls of deeds.

[p. 321] Surah Ya-Sin, peace be upon him. Makkiyya (Meccan), eighty-three verses.

In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿Ya-Sin.﴾ ﴿By the Qur'an, full of wisdom,﴾ ﴿indeed you are among the messengers,﴾ ﴿upon a straight path.﴾ ﴿It is a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful,﴾ ﴿that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless.﴾ ﴿The word has certainly come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles around their necks, reaching to the chins, so they are held with their heads raised.﴾ ﴿And We have placed a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, and covered them, so they do not see.﴾ ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ ﴿You can only warn one who follows the Reminder and fears the Merciful in the unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and a noble reward.﴾ ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forth and their traces, and everything We have enumerated in a clear register.﴾ ﴿And present to them a parable: the people of the town, when the messengers came to it,﴾ ﴿when We sent to them two, and they denied them, so We strengthened them with a third; and they said, "Indeed, we are messengers sent to you."﴾ ﴿They said, "You are only human beings like us, and the Merciful has revealed nothing. You are only lying."﴾ ﴿They said, "Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers to you;﴾ ﴿and our duty is only to deliver the clear message."﴾ ﴿They said, "Indeed, we see you as a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and a painful punishment from us will surely touch you."﴾ ﴿They said, "Your omen is with yourselves. Is it because you were reminded? Rather, you are a transgressing people."﴾ ﴿And there came from the farthest part of the city a man running. He said, "O my people, follow the messengers.﴾ ﴿Follow those who do not ask you for any wage, and who are guided."﴾ ﴿"And why should I not worship He who created me, and to whom you will be returned?﴾ ﴿Shall I take gods besides Him? If the Merciful intends harm for me, their intercession will avail me nothing, nor can they save me.﴾ ﴿Indeed, I would then be in clear error.﴾ ﴿Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me."﴾ ﴿It was said, "Enter Paradise." He said, "Would that my people knew﴾ ﴿of how my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honored."﴾ ﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any army from the heaven, nor were We ever to send down [one].﴾ ﴿It was but one cry, and at once they were extinguished.﴾ ﴿Alas for the servants! No messenger comes to them but that they mock him.﴾ ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, that they do not return to them?﴾ ﴿And all of them, they will surely be brought before Us.

And a sign for them is the dead earth which We have revived and brought forth from it grain, of which they eat.﴾ ﴿And We made in it gardens of palm trees and grapevines, and caused springs to gush forth from it,﴾ ﴿that they may eat of its fruit, and of what their hands produced. Will they not then be thankful?﴾ ﴿Glory be to He who created all the pairs, from what the earth grows, and from themselves, and from what they do not know.﴾ ﴿And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and at once they are in darkness.﴾ ﴿And the sun runs toward its resting place.
