It is reported from Ibn ‘Abbas: there is no tree but that there is fire in it, except the ‘anā. The majority read al-akhḍar; it was also read al-khaḍrā'; the people of the Ḥijāz make the distinguished noun of a collective feminine with tā', and the people of Najd treat certain words as masculine; these are noted in grammar books.

Then He mentioned what is more wondrous and marvelous than the creation of man from a drop and the resurrection of the dead, namely the origination of these great and strange creatures from the transition of nonexistence into existence, and so He said: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81]. The majority read bi-qādir, with the preposition bā' attached to the active participle. Al-Jaḥdarī, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, al-A‘raj, Sallām and Ya‘qūb read yaqdur as an imperfect verb, meaning: whoever was able to create the heavens and the earth, given their greatness, is able to create people. The pronoun in "their like" refers to people, said al-Rummānī. A group of exegetes said it refers to the heavens and the earth, and the pronoun returned to them as to rational beings, since they include rational beings among the angels and the two species of jinn and men. Az-Zamakhshari said: "their like" may have two meanings: that He creates their like in smallness and insignificance in comparison with the heavens and the earth, or that He restores them, since the origins are a like of the beginning and not identical with it. End. He says: the return is the very same as the beginning; if it were a like of it, it would not be called a restoration, but a new origination. The majority read al-Khallāq with the intensive form, because of the abundance of His creatures. Al-Ḥasan, al-Jaḥdarī, Mālik ibn Dīnār and Zayd ibn ‘Alī read al-Khāliq as an active participle.

﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82]: the explanation of this sentence has already preceded, and the difference regarding fa-yakūnu as to reading in the accusative or nominative has been noted.

﴿So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [Ya-Sin: 83]: a general declaration of His exaltedness above all deficiencies. The majority read malakūt; Ṭalḥa and al-A‘mash read malaka, on the pattern of shajara; its meaning is controlling everything and having power over it. It was also read mamlaka, on the pattern of maf‘ala, and malik. The meaning is that He disposes of it as He wills and decrees. The majority read turja‘ūn in the passive voice; Zayd ibn ‘Alī read it in the active voice.

The most excellent of the benefits here, and its superiority, is in His words ﴿and He made for you from the skins of livestock﴾ [An-Nahl: 80] and so on. ﴿They cannot help them﴾ [Ya-Sin: 75], i.e., the gods cannot help their worshippers; this is the apparent meaning. When they took them as gods to seek help through them, God answered them that they have no power to help them. Ibn ‘Aṭiyya said: It is possible that the pronoun in ﴿they cannot﴾ refers to the disbelievers and in "their help" refers to the idols. End. The apparent meaning is that the pronoun in "and they" refers to what is apparent in ﴿they cannot﴾, i.e., the gods are for the disbelievers a host brought forth [to be punished] in the Hereafter at the reckoning, by way of rebuke and retribution. He called them a host because they are prepared for the retribution of their worshippers and for reproach, or they are brought forth for their punishment because they will be made fuel for the Fire. It was said: It is also permissible that the pronoun in "and they" refers to the disbelievers and in "for them" refers to the idols, i.e., they, the idols, are a host brought forth, zealously attached to them, bewildered, defending them, meaning in this world, and yet they cannot—i.e., the disbelievers cannot—support one another. This statement is built on the premise that the pronoun in "they cannot" refers to the disbelievers.

Then God consoled His Prophet by His words ﴿So let not their saying grieve you﴾ [Ya-Sin: 76], i.e., do not be concerned by their denial, their harm and their harshness, and He warned the disbelievers by His words ﴿We know what they conceal and what they reveal﴾ [Ya-Sin: 76], so We will requite them for that.
